node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Ratio language
node.description: Use ratio language to describe multiplicative comparisons between quantities.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Part part ratios
node.description: Represent and interpret ratios comparing one part of a situation with another part.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Part whole ratios
node.description: Represent and interpret ratios comparing a part with the whole quantity.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Ratio notation
node.description: Read and write ratios using colon notation, words and ordered pairs of quantities.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Equivalent ratios
node.description: Generate and recognise ratios that preserve the same multiplicative relationship.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Ratio tables
node.description: Use tables of related pairs to organise and generate equivalent ratios.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Double number lines
node.description: Use aligned number lines to represent equivalent ratios and rate relationships.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rates with units
node.description: Interpret rates as comparisons of quantities with different units.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Unit rates
node.description: Find and use rates per one unit to compare and solve problems.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Proportional relationships
node.description: Recognise relationships in which one quantity is a constant multiple of another.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Scale factor in ratios
node.description: Use scale factors to move between equivalent ratio pairs and proportional quantities.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Proportional equations
node.description: Represent proportional relationships using equations involving a constant multiplier.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Constant of proportionality
node.description: Identify and interpret the constant multiplier in a proportional relationship.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Direct variation graphs
node.description: Represent proportional relationships as graphs through the origin.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Scale drawings
node.description: Use proportional reasoning to interpret and create scale drawings and maps.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Proportion problem solving
node.description: Solve contextual problems involving equivalent ratios, rates and proportional relationships.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Ratio compares quantities
node.description: A ratio compares two quantities multiplicatively rather than by their additive difference.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Ratio order matters
node.description: Changing the order of the quantities in a ratio changes which comparison is being described.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Equivalent ratios preserve relationship
node.description: Equivalent ratios preserve the same multiplicative relationship between quantities.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Unit rate is per one
node.description: A unit rate gives the amount of one quantity for one unit of another quantity.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rates include units
node.description: Rates compare quantities measured in different units and should keep those units visible.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Proportional relationship has constant multiplier
node.description: In a proportional relationship, one quantity is always the same multiplier times the other quantity.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Scale factor preserves ratio
node.description: Scaling both quantities in a ratio by the same nonzero factor preserves the relationship.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Ratio tables show pairs
node.description: Ratio tables organise pairs of values that preserve a ratio or proportional relationship.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Double number lines align quantities
node.description: Double number lines align related quantities so equivalent ratios can be read and scaled.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Proportional equations represent relationship
node.description: An equation such as y = kx can represent a proportional relationship between quantities.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Additive difference used as ratio
node.description: Learner uses the difference between quantities when the situation requires a multiplicative ratio comparison.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Reversing ratio order
node.description: Learner reverses the order of quantities in a ratio and changes the meaning of the comparison.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Equivalent ratios made by adding
node.description: Learner creates equivalent ratios by adding the same amount to both quantities instead of multiplying by the same factor.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Unit rate without units
node.description: Learner calculates a rate but drops the units, making the comparison ambiguous.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: All linear relationships are proportional
node.description: Learner assumes any straight-line or constant-change relationship is proportional, even when it does not pass through the origin or use a constant multiplier from zero.

edge.rationale: Ratio language is foundational for ratio and rate work.
Part-part ratios are a core form of ratio comparison.
Part-whole ratios are related to fractions and support ratio interpretation.
Ratio notation is central to representing ratio comparisons.
Equivalent ratios are central to reasoning with ratios and rates.
Ratio tables are a core representation for equivalent ratio pairs.
Double number lines practise ratio and rate scaling visually.
Rates with units are a core part of the ratio and rate area.
Unit rates are central for comparing and solving rate problems.
Proportional relationships are the core object of proportional reasoning.
Scale factors are central to preserving proportional relationships.
Equations represent proportional relationships symbolically.
The constant of proportionality captures the multiplicative relationship.
Graphs through the origin are a key representation of direct proportion.
Scale drawings apply proportional reasoning in measurement and spatial contexts.
Problem solving directly practises proportional reasoning across contexts.
Ratio language depends on comparing quantities multiplicatively rather than additively.
edge.failure_signal: Learner describes only how many more rather than how many times as many.

edge.rationale: Part-part ratios require identifying two quantities to compare using ratio language.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot state which two parts are being compared.

edge.rationale: Part-whole ratios require identifying a part and the total whole being compared.
edge.failure_signal: Learner confuses part-part and part-whole comparisons.

edge.rationale: Ratio notation requires identifying the ordered quantities in a ratio comparison.
edge.failure_signal: Learner writes a colon form without preserving the order of quantities.

edge.rationale: Equivalent ratios require interpreting the ratio being scaled or compared.
edge.failure_signal: Learner changes one term or adds the same amount to both terms.

edge.rationale: Ratio tables organise equivalent ratio pairs generated by scaling.
edge.failure_signal: Learner creates rows that do not preserve the ratio relationship.

edge.rationale: Double number lines and ratio tables both align equivalent pairs, with number lines adding spatial magnitude.
edge.failure_signal: Learner misaligns corresponding quantities across the two number lines.

edge.rationale: Rates compare two quantities, usually with different units, using ratio language.
edge.failure_signal: Learner gives a number without identifying the two measured quantities.

edge.rationale: A unit rate is a rate expressed per one unit of one quantity.
edge.failure_signal: Learner calculates a quotient but cannot say per one what.

edge.rationale: Proportional relationships preserve equivalent ratios across all corresponding pairs.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats a constant additive difference as proportional.

edge.rationale: Scale factors generate equivalent ratios by multiplying both quantities by the same factor.
edge.failure_signal: Learner adds the same amount instead of scaling both quantities multiplicatively.

edge.rationale: Equations for proportional relationships require recognising the constant multiplicative relationship.
edge.failure_signal: Learner writes an equation that fits one pair but not the proportional relationship.

edge.rationale: The constant of proportionality is the multiplier in a proportional equation.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot interpret k in y = kx as a rate or scale factor.

edge.rationale: Direct variation graphs represent proportional relationships and their constant multiplier.
edge.failure_signal: Learner identifies any straight line as proportional without checking the origin or multiplier.

edge.rationale: Scale drawings use scale factors to preserve proportional lengths.
edge.failure_signal: Learner adds fixed lengths instead of multiplying all lengths by the same scale factor.

edge.rationale: Many proportion problems can be solved by unit-rate or equivalent-ratio reasoning.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot decide whether to use a unit rate, scale factor or equivalent ratio table.
